Muuns'll take you for everything you've got, but they never cheat.|[[Nal Kenuun]] and [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]]|<ref name="Rebel Force: Target">''[[Rebel Force: Target]]''</ref>}}
'''Muuns''' were a thin, tall [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] [[Species/Legends|species]] from the mineral-rich [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Muunilinst/Legends|Muunilinst]], though they also dwelled on the frozen world of [[Scipio/Legends|Scipio]]. The founders of the [[InterGalactic Banking Clan/Legends|InterGalactic Banking Clan]], the largest banking organization in the galaxy, Muuns were known throughout the galaxy for their excellent financial and mathematical skills. Seeking economic stability, the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] exempted Muuns from their wide-spread non-Human persecution, in order to utilize Muuns and their economic finesse.

==Biology, appearance, and traits==
{{Quote|If there is anything the Muun detest more than wasteful spending it is nonconformity.|[[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]]|<ref name="Darth Plagueis">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref>}}
[[File:Muun.jpg|thumb|left|150px|A typical Muun.]]
Muuns were tall and gaunt humanoids with thin bodies and elongated heads with hairless and smooth craniums.<ref name="Darth Plagueis" /> They also had pasty-white/pale pink to grey skin, most likely because the vast majority of the species reluctant to travel, even on-planet, and usually stayed indoors. Muuns also had tiny ears in the middle of the sides of their heads. In addition,<ref name="NEGAS">''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''</ref> they had humped noses<ref name="Darth Plagueis" /> and slim mouths. Muun voices often sound nasal due to their small noses. Muuns had long arms and legs, making them appear very gaunt. They also had very thin waists and long, thin fingers. Members of the species also had three hearts, one normal heart and two that were consciously controlled, a trait often used to increase blood flow in low temperatures. This also may have contributed to a longer life-span.<ref name="NEGAS" />

Muuns were extremely intelligent, and both greedy and cautious when it came to business ventures. They were lured to profitable and vulnerable economic situations or opportunities, yet took long thought before committing themselves to a business deal. Muuns' talent with money stemmed from their extremely valuable mathematical and statistical skills. Muun children were known to calculate complex mathematical formulas as quickly as most adults of other species could. In addition to being greedy and cautious, Muuns also deemed themselves to be a reserved, mature species, capable of controlling their emotions, and deemed other species as immature, and felt no remorse in exploiting them, if need required them to do so. Muuns possessed a drive to compete with other races and even among themselves, which also contributed to higher rates of economic output anywhere Muuns were located. Muuns also had a fundamental respect for fairness and justice, however, and regarded a contract as almost a sacred trust. Muuns were known to always follow the letter of the law, though often not the spirit.<ref name="NEGAS" />

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|Banking clan investments. Or lawyering. That's all the Muuns do, Captain.|A Klatooinian on Darth Plagueis{{'}} activities|<ref name="Darth Plagueis">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref>}}
The Muuns believed in tradition and established a culture based on merit and intelligence. A class-hierarchy developed around this worldview, valuing financiers, [[Lawyer/Legends|lawyers]], [[Engineer/Legends|engineers]], and [[Diplomat/Legends|diplomats]] as the highest levels of society. Commoners rarely left the surface of their planet as upward mobility was limited, reserved for only the most gifted of children who passed rigorous examinations.<ref name="NEGAS" />

[[File:IGBCMuunilinst.jpg|thumb|210px|Muuns in [[Harnaidan]], the center of economic activity on [[Muunilinst/Legends|Muunilinst]].]]

Muun culture, indeed, Muun life, revolved around economy and finance. Intense competition among co-workers encouraged economic growth, increased production, and superior work ethic. Since Muuns tended to shy away from fighting and physical pursuits, Muun society used alternative means for their planet's protection, using their vast financial resources to purchase massive floating defense platforms to defend their planet from attack. The [[InterGalactic Banking Clan/Legends|InterGalactic Banking Clan]] (IGBC), a largely Muun-run organization, was known to utilize hired mercenaries to enforce their policies and collect payments and debts.<ref name="NEGAS" />

Muun reliance on mathematics leaked over into [[Muun (language)/Legends|their language]], which was a collection of ''um'' and ''eh'' sounds of varying pitch, similar in some ways to [[Binary/Legends|Binary]].<ref name="NEGAS" />

==History==
====Humble Beginnings====
{{Quote|I'm willing to concede Master Jinn's point that the Muuns have cornered the market on finance, if he is willing to concede that the Jedi have cornered the market on ethics.|[[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Hego Damask]] verbally spars with [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]]|<ref name="Darth Plagueis" />}}
[[File:SanHillPledge-AOTC.png|thumb|left|250px|[[InterGalactic Banking Clan/Legends|InterGalactic Banking Clan]] [[Chairman/Legends|Chairman]] [[San Hill/Legends|San Hill]].]]
The Muuns hailed from [[Muunilinst/Legends|Muunilinst]]. Early in their history, the ancient Muuns started out as farmers and fisherfolk who did not know how favored their planet and it's vast mineral and metal resources could be to the galactic economy until interstellar travel had become commonplace. Had the Muun's early millenia of expansion not been a peaceful and undisturbed time, Muunilinst would likely have been lost to the military might of invaders but the Muun people had managed to resist all attempts at exploitation and remained the masters of their own fate.<ref name="Darth Plagueis" />

Once the Muuns understood how to utilize the near-endless supply of precious metals produced by their homeworld's volcanic [[Smoker]]s, Muunilinst became a source of inexhaustible wealth for the Muun people and made them indispensable in the galactic financial sector.<ref name="Darth Plagueis" />

====Cornering the market====
With backing of their planetary wealth and their unique mathematical instincts, the Muuns founded the InterGalactic Banking Clan, which came to span not only the galaxy, but smaller satellite galaxies as well. Because of its immense mineral wealth, Muunilinst was used to give weight to the [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|Galactic credit]], making its importance in galactic society almost incomparable to many, if not most [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]].<ref name="Darth Plagueis" />

Throughout the time of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], Muuns had a knack for funding potentially profitable enterprises throughout its [[Sector/Legends|sector]], regardless of ethics or loyalty. Muunilinst provided much of the funding for the nearby [[Human/Legends|Human]] colony world of [[Bastion/Legends|Sartinaynian]], which, ironically, broke away from the Republic because of anti-alien sentiments. The banking clans of Muunilinst were uninterested in these prejudices. They funded colonies, trade guilds, and corporations all along the [[Braxant Run/Legends|Braxant Run]]. At some point in their history the Muuns also colonized the planet of [[Mygeeto/Legends|Mygeeto]], which, much like Muunilinst itself, would become wealthy as an important financial center.<ref name="Darth Plagueis" />

[[Scipio/Legends|Scipio]] also became a major hub for the Muuns and Banking Clan,<ref name="Crisis">{{TCW|Crisis at the Heart}}</ref> holding the [[Main Vault/Legends|Main Vault]] and being the meeting place for the [[Core Five/Legends|Core Five]].<ref name="Endless Vigil" /> Eventually, Scipio,<ref name="SS">{{TCW|Senate Spy}}</ref> Muunilinst, and Sartinaynian came to be member worlds in the Republic, and Muunilinst became one of the greatest financial powers in the galaxy. The power and influence of the Banking Clan was largely unchecked as the Republic fell into decline and corruption, and with the looming threat of the breakdown of law and order, the IGBC invested in thousands of [[IG-227 Hailfire-class droid tank/Legends|''Hailfire'' droids]] to discourage customers from defaulting on their loans.

===Clone Wars===
{{Quote|I've always hated your kind.|[[Reija Momen]] to [[Pors Tonith/Legends|Pors Tonith]]|<ref name="Jedi Trial">''[[Jedi Trial]]''</ref>}}
Prior to the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], IGBC [[Chairman/Legends|Chairman]] [[San Hill/Legends|San Hill]] was approached by the leader of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist movement]], [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]]. San Hill helped finance the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], believing it very plausible that the Confederacy could conquer the Republic. San Hill also used secret Banking Clan codes used for transferring bank statements and depositing money to clients to establish the [[Hyper-Communications Cartel/Legends|Shadowfeed Network]], a secret Confederate analogue to the [[HoloNet/Legends|HoloNet]], used to distribute propaganda to the galaxy. It was also used as a means to allow Confederate leaders to transmit untraceable and untappable messages to their subordinates, making the Banking Clan an invaluable member of the Confederacy.

[[File:MarchingMuuns-CW20.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Captured Muuns in the city of [[Harnaidan]] on [[Muunilinst/Legends|Muunilinst]] being escorted by [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]].]]
Consistent with its reputation for playing both sides against the middle, Muunilinst simultaneously backed the Republic and the Confederacy during the Clone Wars. Alliances with the Confederacy, however, led to Separatist forces building [[Droid/Legends|droid]] factories and munitions depots on Muunilinst, over the objections of the native Muuns. Despite its economic importance, the Republic was left with no other option than to invade Muunilinst and destroy the Confederate strongholds. This led to a series of ruinous battles.

During the [[Battle of Muunilinst/Legends|Battle of Muunilinst]] in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], and [[Voolvif Monn]] retook the planet for the Republic, but at great cost. The battle devastated the Muun cities, sparing none, and led the galaxy to the brink of financial ruin.

===Later history===
Muunilinst later became the financial center of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] harbored no fondness for [[Non-huMan|non-Humans]], but the mineral riches of Muunilinst were too important for the stability of Imperial credit and he even had a [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Sith Master]] that was a Muun, the last non-Human to rule the [[Sith Order]] before the Republic was dissolved. Muuns' lending and business operations were hampered by harsh Imperial decrees and the presence of Imperial monitors stationed throughout the world's financial institutions. Muunilinst was no more loyal to the Empire than it was to the Republic or Confederacy, but found it expedient not to undermine Imperial power, reasoning that, no matter the outcome of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the victor would be forced to keep doing business with the Muuns and the IGBC. It remained part of the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]] during the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] years, protected by two [[Golan III Space Defense NovaGun|Golan III battle platforms]]. Amazingly, but again consistent with their reputation, even while a part of the Imperial Remnant, Muunilinst still became the guarantor of the New Republic credit. This infuriated the [[Moff/Legends|Moffs]], but they were powerless to move against the IGBC without destabilizing the Imperial credit.

During the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], the alien intruders attacked the Imperial Remnant. In a coordinated strike, the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] decimated the forces protecting Muunilinst. The planet itself was bombarded from orbit, reducing it to a wasteland from which the Yuuzhan Vong plucked any survivors for use as [[Slavery/Legends|slave]] labor. By [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]], Muunilinst had recovered.<ref name="R">''[[Legacy of the Force: Revelation]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Composite-eyed_race.jpg|thumb|A possible first appearance of the Muuns in ''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special]]'' (to the left of [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]])]]
The character of San Hill was created for the movie [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']], released in [[May]] [[2002]], as the leader of the InterGalactic Banking Clan.<ref name="Attack of the Clones">{{Film|II}}</ref> His name first appeared in a [[February]] 2002 [[HoloNet News Vol. 531 45|article]] on the [[HoloNet News (original website)|HoloNet News website]],<ref name="HoloNet News Datanet Propaganda">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|45|business/13228_2.html|Datanet Propaganda the Real Deal?}}</ref> and a picture of both him and Lo Vapeet appeared in another HoloNet News [[HoloNet News Vol. 531 47|article]] [[March|one month later]]. That article also established that the Banking Clan was headquartered on Muunilinst,<ref name="HoloNet News Currency Upheavals">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|47|business/13314_1.html|Currency Upheavals Deliver Profits to IBC}}</ref> a planet that had been introduced in [[Timothy Zahn]]'s [[1997]] novel ''[[Specter of the Past]]'' as a financial world.<ref name="Specter">''[[Specter of the Past]]''</ref> San Hill's species was not named in Episode II, its novelization, nor in much of the movie's supplementary reference books, and instead was first established in [[Galactic Power Brokers]], an article featured in the [[Star Wars Gamer 10|tenth issue]] of ''[[Star Wars Gamer]]'' magazine (May 2002).<ref name="Galactic Power Brokers">{{GamerCite|10|Galactic Power Brokers}}</ref>

Two previous [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] works contain characters who could easily be [[Retroactive continuity|retconned]] as Muuns. The first, the [[The Story of the Faithful Wookiee|animated segment]] of ''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special]]'', contains two unnamed characters on [[Panna/Legends|Panna]] who look like Muuns. When asked if it was possible that the characters were Muuns, [[Leland Chee]] said, "Sure."<ref name="HCTq">{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=152583&start=01005#15930568|thread=Holocron continuity database questions|user=[[Leland Chee|Leland Y Chee]]|date=2006-11-15|time=9:17 AM}}</ref> Another possible Muun is [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] [[Graemon]], an Imperial-allied banker who is described as "a lean man wearing the traditional Muunilinsti banker's shawl and pendant" in ''Specter of the Past''.<ref name="Specter" />

The [[2014]] [[Fantasy Flight Games]] sourcebook ''[[Endless Vigil]]'' incorrectly states [[Scipio/Legends|Scipio]] as the Muun homeworld, instead of Muunilinst,<ref name="Endless Vigil" /> which the vast majority of sources state is their homeworld.<ref name="UAA" /><ref name="Darth Plagueis" /><ref name="NEGAS" /> In ''[[Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption]]'', Muuns are incorrectly depicted as being identical to Humans in loading screens.
